title: Demolition Roof Work: Guard Skylights Before You Step
summary: A demolition laborer died after stepping backward onto a skylight while removing roofing. He fell about 19 feet to a concrete floor and had no fall protection or fall protection training. Guard skylights and get trained before roof work.
talking_points: A 44-year-old laborer was removing roofing components. He walked backward onto a skylight, it broke, and he fell about 19 feet. He was not using personal fall arrest equipment and had not been given fall protection training by the demolition employer.
OSHA requires protection from falling through skylights more than 6 feet above a lower level. Use a personal fall arrest system, skylight covers, or a guardrail system around them.
Guardrails or screens on all skylights should go up before roofing work begins and stay until all work is complete.
Skylight covers must support at least twice the weight of workers, equipment, and materials placed on them. They must be secured against wind, equipment, and workers, and marked HOLE or COVER.
Guardrails, covers, and safety nets are preferred over personal fall arrest systems. Use fall arrest when the other controls are being installed or are not workable.
Do a job hazard analysis or pre-task plan before roof work. Find the hazards and the fall protection each task needs.
Training should be in a language and form you understand. Speak up if you have not been trained.
On a multi-employer site, each employer may have duties for your safety. Ask who is in charge of fall protection.
site_hazards_to_check: Skylights in the roof with no railing, screen, or cover
Roof edges and openings exposed during roofing removal
Workers walking backward or looking away from the surface behind them
No harnesses, anchors, or fall protection training for the crew
Unclear responsibility for safety between the demolition contractor and subcontractors
discussion_questions: Where are the skylights and openings on this roof, and how are they protected?
What fall protection will each person use on the roof?
Has everyone been trained, in a language they understand, on fall hazards for this job?
